mechanism: Restoration-budget-derived per-tenant KV reservations coupled to preemption victim choice
prior_comparison: Generic deadline/prefill policy overlaps H01/B200-R7b/LP63; reservation accounting not identical to CF59/HM65/AV68 or bounded-tail/prefix-admission mechanisms. No novelty certification.
reason: No tenant-policy workload or restoration-cost exposure established; direct cache-only port misses active request preemption and hybrid cache accounting. Higher integration burden than presently actionable narrow candidates.
reopen_when: Existing target traces identify tenant mapping, cross-tenant preemption/recomputation and deadline violations attributable to cache pressure.
Define sharing/ownership and restoration cost across hybrid cache groups; source-safe victim integration preserving output/cache lifecycle.
next_falsifier: Check retained request/metrics provenance for tenant identity and preemption-attributed stalls; do not fabricate tenants from API frontend client_index or prefix IDs. No new GPU harness required.
single_tenant_adaptation: Per-client prioritization degenerates, but protecting inactive cache by restoration budget can still be a cost-aware retention arm. It trades allocatable headroom and possibly preemption; prefix classes need explicit shared ownership and are not automatically tenants.
